info.title: FixFlow API
info.description: Field service work order management API for dispatchers and technicians.

post.summary: Log in with email and password
post.description: Returns a short-lived JWT access token and a refresh token that starts a new session. Wrong credentials and locked out accounts return the same 401 response, so the endpoint does not reveal whether an account exists. Requests are rate limited per client IP address.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new token pair
post.description: Rotates the refresh token: the submitted token is revoked and a new access token and refresh token are returned. A refresh token that was already used can be exchanged again within a short grace period after its rotation (30 seconds by default) while its session is active, for example by a second browser tab or by a mobile client that lost the previous response; the earlier replacement stays valid. Submitting an already used refresh token after the grace period revokes every token of that session, which forces the user to log in again. A refresh token of a deactivated account is rejected and its session is revoked. Requests are rate limited per client IP address.

post.summary: Log out and revoke the current session
post.description: Revokes the submitted refresh token together with every token of its session. An access token is not required, so a client whose access token has already expired can still end its session. Access tokens issued before stay valid until they expire. The response is 204 also when the refresh token is unknown. Requests are rate limited per client IP address.
Creates an account with the given role and initial password. Only administrators can create accounts; there is no public registration.

get.description: Returns one page of user accounts ordered by full name and email, optionally limited to one role and to active or deactivated accounts, for example role=Technician&isActive=true when a dispatcher chooses a technician for a work order. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting from 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Number of users per page, from 1 to 100.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Role of the listed users: Admin, Dispatcher or Technician.

parameters.name: isActive
parameters.description: When true, lists only active accounts, for example when choosing a technician for a work order; when false, only deactivated accounts.

get.description: Returns the identifier, email, full name, role and active status of the account that owns the access token. Available to every signed-in user.

post.summary: Change the password of the current user
post.description: Replaces the password of the signed-in user after checking the current one. All refresh tokens of the user are revoked, which signs out other devices, and a new token pair is returned for the calling device. Access tokens issued before stay valid until they expire. Requests are rate limited per client IP address.

Blocks signing in to the account and revokes all its refresh tokens. Access tokens issued before stay valid until they expire. A technician with assigned or in-progress work orders cannot be deactivated until the work orders are unassigned or completed, and administrators cannot deactivate their own account. Deactivating an already deactivated account has no effect. Available to administrators.
Allows a deactivated account to sign in again with its current password. Activating an active account has no effect. Available to administrators.

post.summary: Reset the password of a user account
post.description: Replaces the password of any account, for example when the user forgot it, lifts a lockout after failed sign-ins and revokes all refresh tokens of the account. Access tokens issued before stay valid until they expire. Available to administrators.

put.description: Changes the first and last name of any account. The email, role and password are not changed. Available to administrators.

get.description: Returns the identifier, email, full name, role and active status of any account, for example to fill the form for editing the account. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

post.description: Creates a client with a postal address and contact details. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

get.description: Returns one page of active clients ordered by name. Archived clients are not listed. The optional search matches a fragment of the client name regardless of letter case.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting from 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Number of clients per page, from 1 to 100.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive fragment of the client name.

get.description: Returns a client by identifier, including archived clients so that historical work orders keep their client details.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

put.description: Replaces the name, address and contact details of an active client. Archived clients cannot be modified. The If-Match header must carry the ETag of the client; a client changed in the meantime is rejected with 412. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: ETag of the resource returned by the last read or change. A different current version is rejected with 412.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

post.description: Hides the client from lists while keeping it and its history available by identifier. All active devices of the client are archived in the same operation and no new devices can be added to it. Archiving an already archived client has no effect. Available to dispatchers and administrators.
Registers a device of an active client. The serial number is trimmed, stored in upper case and must be unique, also among archived devices. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

get.description: Returns one page of active devices ordered by serial number, each with the name of the client that owns it. Archived devices are not listed. The optional client filter limits the list to devices of one client, and the optional search matches a fragment of the serial number, model or manufacturer regardless of letter case.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting from 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Number of devices per page, from 1 to 100.

parameters.name: clientId
parameters.description: Identifier of the client whose devices are listed.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive fragment of the serial number, model or manufacturer.

get.description: Returns a device by identifier, including archived devices so that historical work orders keep their device details.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

put.description: Replaces the serial number, model, manufacturer and installation date of an active device. The owning client cannot be changed and archived devices cannot be modified. The If-Match header must carry the ETag of the device; a device changed in the meantime is rejected with 412. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: ETag of the resource returned by the last read or change. A different current version is rejected with 412.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

post.description: Hides the device from lists while keeping it and its history available by identifier. The serial number of an archived device stays reserved. Archiving an already archived device has no effect. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

get.summary: List the service history of a device
get.description: Returns one page of work orders of a device, newest first, with ties ordered by identifier. Each work order comes with the name of the assigned technician and the number of its service entries. Dispatchers and administrators see all work orders of the device, including archived devices. Technicians see only work orders assigned to them; a device without such work orders is reported as not found.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting from 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Number of work orders per page, from 1 to 100.

post.description: Creates an unassigned work order in the New status for an active device. The due date must be in the future. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

get.description: Returns one page of work orders sorted by the requested field and direction, by default by due date ascending, with ties ordered by identifier so that pages neither skip nor repeat work orders. Each work order comes with the serial number and model of the device, the client name, address and contact details, and the technician name and email. The list can be filtered by one or more statuses, technician, device, client, overdue flag and due date range, and searched by a fragment of the work order number, description, serial number or client name. Technicians only see work orders assigned to them.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting from 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Number of work orders per page, from 1 to 100.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Statuses of the listed work orders. Repeat the parameter to list work orders in any of several statuses, for example status=Assigned&status=InProgress.

parameters.name: technicianId
parameters.description: Identifier of the assigned technician.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Identifier of the serviced device.

parameters.name: clientId
parameters.description: Identifier of the client whose devices were serviced.

parameters.name: isOverdue
parameters.description: When true, lists only overdue work orders; when false, only work orders that are not overdue.

parameters.name: dueFrom
parameters.description: First day of the due date range, inclusive, as a calendar date in the Europe/Warsaw time zone.

parameters.name: dueTo
parameters.description: Last day of the due date range, inclusive, as a calendar date in the Europe/Warsaw time zone.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive fragment of the work order number, the fault description, the device serial number or the client name.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Field the work orders are sorted by. Priority is sorted by importance from Low to Critical and status in lifecycle order from New to Invoiced.

parameters.name: sortDirection
parameters.description: Direction of sorting: Asc for ascending, Desc for descending.

get.description: Returns a work order by identifier. Technicians can only get work orders assigned to them; other work orders are reported as not found.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

put.description: Replaces the description, priority and due date of a work order without changing its status or technician. A changed due date must be in the future. Completed and invoiced work orders cannot be edited. The If-Match header must carry the ETag of the work order; a work order changed in the meantime is rejected with 412. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: ETag of the resource returned by the last read or change. A different current version is rejected with 412.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

post.summary: Assign a technician to a work order
post.description: Assigns an active user with the Technician role to a work order in the New status and moves it to Assigned, optionally changing the deadline in the same operation. To change the technician of an assigned work order, use reassign. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

post.summary: Move an assigned work order to another technician or date
post.description: Changes the technician and optionally the deadline of a work order in the Assigned status in one operation, so the work order is never left unassigned in between. The same technician can be passed to change only the deadline. Work orders in progress cannot be reassigned. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

post.summary: Unassign the technician from a work order
post.description: Removes the technician from a work order in the Assigned status and moves it back to New. Work that has already started cannot be unassigned. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

post.summary: Start work on a work order
post.description: Moves a work order assigned to the calling technician from Assigned to InProgress. A technician can have only one work order in progress at a time. The body is optional: without it the work starts at the server time, with startedAt the work starts at the time given by the client, for example recorded offline. Starting a work order that the same technician has already started, completed or invoiced returns its current state without changes, so a queued start can be safely sent again; startedAt is then not compared. Work orders of other technicians are reported as not found. Available to technicians only.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

post.description: Moves a work order from InProgress to Completed. The work order must have at least one service entry. The body is optional: without it the work order is completed at the server time, with completedAt at the time given by the client, for example recorded offline. Completing a work order that is already completed or invoiced returns its current state without changes, so a queued completion can be safely sent again; completedAt is then not compared. After completion no service entries can be added and the work order cannot be edited. Available to the assigned technician and, as a fallback, to dispatchers and administrators; work orders of other technicians are reported as not found.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

post.summary: Mark a work order as invoiced
post.description: Moves a completed work order to Invoiced, which is the final status. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

get.description: Returns the service protocol of a completed or invoiced work order as a PDF document in Polish, named after the work order number, for example protokol-ZL-2026-0042.pdf. The protocol lists the client, the device, all service entries with work time, the net used parts with amounts in PLN and fields for signatures, with the client's signature image when it was given at completion. Technicians can only download protocols of work orders assigned to them; other work orders are reported as not found.

get.summary: List the history of a work order
get.description: Returns the changes of a work order, oldest first: creation, edits, assignment, reassignment and unassignment of the technician, start, completion and invoicing, each with the time, the user who made the change and the technician and deadline after the change. Repeated start or completion requests do not add events. Technicians can only get the history of work orders assigned to them; other work orders are reported as not found.

post.description: Adds a part to the warehouse catalog with an initial stock quantity. The catalog number is trimmed, stored in upper case and must be unique, also among archived parts. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

get.description: Returns one page of active parts with their current stock quantities, ordered by name and catalog number. Archived parts are not listed. The optional search matches a fragment of the name or catalog number regardless of letter case, and the optional stock filter limits the list to parts in stock or out of stock.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting from 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Number of parts per page, from 1 to 100.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive fragment of the name or catalog number.

parameters.name: inStock
parameters.description: When true, lists only parts with at least one unit in stock, for example when a technician picks used parts; when false, only parts that are out of stock.

get.description: Returns a part with its current stock quantity by identifier, including archived parts so that historical service entries keep their part details.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

put.description: Replaces the name, catalog number and unit price of an active part. The stock quantity is not changed and archived parts cannot be modified. A new price applies only to parts used afterwards. The If-Match header must carry the ETag of the part; a part changed in the meantime is rejected with 412. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: ETag of the resource returned by the last read or change. A different current version is rejected with 412.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

post.description: Hides the part from lists and prevents it from being used in new service entries, while keeping it available by identifier. The catalog number of an archived part stays reserved and its stock can still be replenished. Archiving an already archived part has no effect. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

Increases the stock quantity of a part by the number of delivered units, also for archived parts. A delivery registered at the same time as another stock change is rejected with a conflict and can be retried. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

ETag.description: Current version of the resource, to be sent in If-Match when changing it.

post.description: Adds a work entry or a correction entry to a work order in progress assigned to the calling technician. Parts used in a work entry are taken from stock at their current price and the entry is rejected if the stock would drop below zero. A correction returns parts to stock, at most the net quantity used on the work order, at the price of their last use. Entries cannot be changed or deleted. Work orders of other technicians are reported as not found. Available to technicians only. When the request carries an identifier of an entry already added by the same technician to the same work order, the stored entry is returned with status 200 without taking parts from stock again and without checking the work order status, so a queued entry can be safely sent again even after the work order was completed; the request content is not compared. An identifier used on another work order or by another technician is rejected with a conflict.

get.summary: List service entries of a work order
get.description: Returns all work and correction entries of a work order, oldest first. Technicians see only entries of work orders assigned to them; other work orders are reported as not found.

Returns one work or correction entry of a work order. Technicians see only entries of work orders assigned to them; other work orders are reported as not found. An entry of a different work order is reported as not found.

put.description: Stores a JPEG photo under an identifier chosen by the client, so the photo address /api/v1/photos/{photoId} is known before the upload and can be put in photoUrls of a service entry created offline. The body is the raw image/jpeg content of at most 1048576 bytes. Available to technicians only. When the identifier was already used by the same technician, the stored photo is kept and returned with status 200, so a queued upload can be safely sent again; the content is not compared. An identifier used by another technician is rejected with a conflict. A technician can upload at most 100 new photos within any 24 hours; further uploads are rejected with a conflict, while resending an already stored photo is still accepted.

get.description: Returns the stored JPEG photo. Available without authentication, so the photo address from photoUrls of a service entry can be used directly as an image source; anyone who knows the address can read the photo. A stored photo never changes, so the response can be cached for a year and carries the photo identifier as ETag; a request with a matching If-None-Match returns 304 without content.

Returns aggregated work order counts read from a single consistent database snapshot: the number of work orders in each status in lifecycle order (including zeros), the number of work orders flagged as overdue (the same criterion as the isOverdue=true filter of the work order list), the number of active parts out of stock (the same criterion as the inStock=false filter of the part list), and the workload of every active technician sorted by full name and email, including technicians without work orders. The current week runs from Monday to Sunday in the Europe/Warsaw time zone; its bounds are returned as calendar dates usable as dueFrom and dueTo of the work order list. Available to dispatchers and administrators.

post.summary: Reset demo data to its initial state
post.description: Deletes all clients, devices, parts, work orders and service entries and recreates the demo data set. Restores the demo dispatcher and technician accounts: configured passwords, active status, no sign-in lockout, and revokes their refresh tokens. Accounts created by administrators are kept. Available to administrators on instances with demo data enabled; otherwise returns 409.

note.description: Description of the performed work or, for a correction, its reason.

isCorrection.description: True for a correction entry that returns parts to stock; false for a work entry.

photoUrls.description: Absolute http or https addresses of photos, at most 10.

workStartedAt.description: Time when the work started; required for a work entry and not allowed for a correction. Cannot be earlier than the start of the work order.

workFinishedAt.description: Time when the work finished; required for a work entry and not allowed for a correction. Must be after the start and not later than the server time plus the allowed clock skew.

latitude.description: Latitude of the place where the work started, from -90 to 90; optional, given together with longitude and not allowed for a correction.

longitude.description: Longitude of the place where the work started, from -180 to 180; optional, given together with latitude and not allowed for a correction.

parts.description: Parts used in a work entry or returned in a correction, at most 20, each part at most once. Required for a correction.

id.description: Optional identifier of the entry chosen by the client, for example by an offline queue. Sending an entry again with the same identifier returns the stored entry instead of adding a new one; when omitted, the server assigns the identifier.

AddServiceEntryRequest.description: New service entry of a work order in progress. A work entry records performed work and used parts; a correction entry returns wrongly recorded parts to stock and has no work time or location.

technicianId.description: Identifier of a user with the Technician role.

dueDate.description: New UTC deadline; it must be in the future when it differs from the current one. When omitted, the deadline does not change.

Cannot be earlier than the start of the work order or the end of its last work entry and cannot be later than the server time plus the allowed clock skew; a time within the skew is stored as the server time. When omitted, the server time is used.

email.description: Email address of the user account.

fullName.description: First and last name of the user shown in clients instead of the email.

isActive.description: False when an administrator deactivated the account; a deactivated account cannot sign in.

occurredAt.description: UTC time of the change; for start and completion the time given by the technician.

actorId.description: Identifier of the user who made the change; null for changes made by the system, for example demo data.

actorName.description: First and last name of the user who made the change; null for changes made by the system.

technicianId.description: Identifier of the technician assigned after the change; null when no technician is assigned.

technicianName.description: First and last name of the technician assigned after the change; null when no technician is assigned.

dueDate.description: UTC deadline of the work order after the change.

WorkOrderEventResponse.description: Change recorded in the history of a work order.

WorkOrderEventType.description: Kind of change recorded in the history of a work order.

number.description: Readable number of the work order, for example ZL/2026/0042, numbered from 1 in each year of creation in the Europe/Warsaw time zone.

deviceSerialNumber.description: Serial number of the serviced device.

clientId.description: Identifier of the client owning the device.

clientName.description: Name of the client owning the device.

clientAddress.description: Postal address of the client, where the device is serviced.

clientPhone.description: Contact phone number of the client.

status.description: Current status of the work order.

technicianId.description: Identifier of the assigned technician; null when no technician is assigned.

technicianEmail.description: Email of the assigned technician; null when no technician is assigned.

technicianName.description: First and last name of the assigned technician; null when no technician is assigned.

dueDate.description: UTC deadline of the work order.

isOverdue.description: True when the deadline has passed and the work order is neither completed nor invoiced.

createdAt.description: UTC time when the work order was created.

startedAt.description: UTC time when the technician started the work; null before the work is started.

completedAt.description: UTC time when the work order was completed; null before completion.

invoicedAt.description: UTC time when the work order was invoiced; null before invoicing.

WorkOrderListItemResponse.description: Work order on a list, with basic details of its device, client and technician.

number.description: Readable number of the work order, for example ZL/2026/0042, numbered from 1 in each year of creation in the Europe/Warsaw time zone.

deviceSerialNumber.description: Serial number of the serviced device.

clientId.description: Identifier of the client owning the device.

clientName.description: Name of the client owning the device.

clientAddress.description: Postal address of the client, where the device is serviced.

clientPhone.description: Contact phone number of the client.

status.description: Current status. Allowed transitions: New -> Assigned -> InProgress -> Completed -> Invoiced, and Assigned -> New when the technician is unassigned.

technicianId.description: Identifier of the assigned technician; null when no technician is assigned.

technicianEmail.description: Email of the assigned technician; null when no technician is assigned.

technicianName.description: First and last name of the assigned technician; null when no technician is assigned.

dueDate.description: UTC deadline of the work order.

isOverdue.description: True when the deadline has passed and the work order is neither completed nor invoiced. Set by an hourly job and recalculated immediately when the deadline changes.

createdAt.description: UTC time when the work order was created.

startedAt.description: UTC time when the technician started the work; null before the work is started.

completedAt.description: UTC time when the work order was completed; null before completion.

invoicedAt.description: UTC time when the work order was invoiced; null before invoicing.

clientSignaturePhotoId.description: Identifier of the photo of the client's signature given at completion, available at /api/v1/photos/{photoId}; null when no signature was given.

WorkOrderResponse.description: Service work order with basic details of its device, client and technician.

WorkOrderStatus.description: Status of a work order. Allowed transitions: New -> Assigned -> InProgress -> Completed -> Invoiced, and Assigned -> New when the technician is unassigned.

count.description: Number of work orders in the status.

WorkOrderStatusCountResponse.description: Number of work orders in one status.

Bearer.description: Access token returned by the login or refresh endpoint.
